chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Isma'il said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about drinking al-faqqa' (a type of drink/food) so he disliked it with a strong dislike.

key_terms.أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, referring to Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the eighth Imam.
key_terms.اَلْفُقَّاعِ: A type of drink or food, often made from fenugreek seeds or similar ingredients, known in early Islamic times.
key_terms.كَرَاهَةً شَدِيدَةً: Strong dislike, indicating a status of makruh (disliked) in Islamic jurisprudence, rather than haram (forbidden).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on drinking faqqa' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), transmitted via the reliable chain of al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, establishes the ruling on 'al-faqqa'' (a traditional fenugreek-based drink) as strongly disliked (karhatun shadidah). In Shia jurisprudence, this strong dislike often points towards istihbab or at least a recommendation to avoid it unless for medicinal necessity, reflecting the Imam's attention to dietary purity and digestion. The hadith is recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, a primary source for Ja'fari fiqh, highlighting the practical application of prophetic traditions in daily consumption.
